content:
Alex Chen: :rotating_light: apiserver p99 spike in eu-north1, controller-manager restarted 3x in last 10m. seeing GPU attach failures and NVMe IOPS high. tagging @oncall
Priya Singh: same here, noticed etcd leader change at 5267890095. logs show repeated WAL/fsync timeouts.
Priya Singh: ```
kube-apiserver: E0812 12:34:56.789 server.go: request handler timeout
etcd: WAL sync took 1200ms; compaction paused
provisioner: attach timeout for instance gpu-cc-01 (errno=ETIMEDOUT)
```
Mateo Garcia: is this isolated to eu-north1? our cluster-level dashboard only shows a region-local spike. any recent driver/kernel rollouts?
Jun Park: cloud provider maintenance window in eu-north1 starting ~12:20 UTC — saw a status post about degraded NVMe performance on a subset of hosts: https://provider.status/incidents/3392
Alex Chen: provider confirmed degraded iops on some NVMe-backed hosts. diverting non-critical inference traffic to eu-west1 now and scaling down batch jobs to reduce attach pressure.
Priya Singh: can we avoid risky etcd changes. short-term idea: increase etcd election timeout to reduce churn? controller-manager is losing leader lease and bouncing.
Mateo Garcia: short term actions: cordon affected worker hosts, drain GPU pods, move provisioner to alternate AZs. long term: increase pool diversity across zones + warm standby GPUs (cost tradeoff).
Jun Park: @finance FYI cross-region shifts will spike egress and inter-region storage costs if we keep running heavy batches in different regions.
finance-bot: Noted — estimated extra cost for 2h cross-region shift: ~$2.3k (compute+egress). Approve? (react :thinking_face:)
Alex Chen: temporary mitigations applied: reduced kube-apiserver concurrent requests to 200 for now, enabled prefix caching on embeddings route, and rolled back the recent kernel module to a canary subset.
Priya Singh: :thumbsup: I'll add a metric alert for etcd WAL fsync > 500ms and collect heap/pprof from apiserver. starting a short trace capture.
sre-bot: INCIDENT created: INC-2026-1423 — controlplane-degradation-eunorth1 (severity=high)
Jun Park: provider update: NVMe recoveries in progress, ETA ~40m. they may replace hosts if performance doesn't recover.
Mateo Garcia: Agree on policy changes once stable: increase attach timeout from 60s to 120s for cloud attach flakiness, and add autoscaler weights to prefer healthy-zones.
Alex Chen: added runbook link for post-incident follow-up: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/controlplane-storage-degradation
Priya Singh: after draining affected nodes, controller-manager restart count dropped to 0 in last 5m and apiserver p99 is returning to baseline. keeping thread open until provider completes remediation.
Mateo Garcia: leaving monitoring on — will post a summary once provider confirms host replacements or recovery.
Jun Park: update 30m later: provider marked incident resolved; we saw one more leader swap at 5267890148 but stable since. closing on-call actions and scheduling a postmortem prep.
Alex Chen: thanks team. postmortem owners: Priya (lead), Mateo (infra impact), Jun (provider comms). will schedule 1hr review tomorrow.
